entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This petition is filed for quashing of FIR No.370/2022 under Section 498A/406 IPC registered at police station Fatehpur Beri, New Delhi.
2. The marriage between the petitioner and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 13.04.2013 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.

On 28.09.2014 one male child viz.
Master Pravit was born from the wedlock.
However, due to matrimonial discord, the respondent No.2 left her matrimonial home along with her son in May, 2019.
The minor child is still in custody of respondent No.2.
On the complaint of respondent No.2 the aforesaid FIR was registered.
3. On 01.11.2022 the matter was amicably settled between the parties vide Settlement before the Mediation Centre, Saket Courts, New Delhi.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent.
The petitioner agreed to pay an amount of Rs.5.50 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claim of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.

4. The complainant/respondent No.2 is present and has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer and states the matter has been settled with the petitioner and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed against the petitioner as she has no claim left against the petitioner.

It is submitted both the petitioner and respondent No.2 shall abide by the terms of the settlement dated 01.11.2022 and Manoj Prasad vs The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89897006/
1 also in respect of custody and visiting rights.

entities.text: Manoj Prasad vs The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The learned ASC for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

6. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioner.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioner as it would never entail in conviction of petitioner.
7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.370/2022 under Section 498A/406 IPC registered at police station Fatehpur Beri, New Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
8. This order would not come in the way in case the child may exercise any right against his father/guardian in future.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
